messages.subject: minimum detection probability
parts:
Hi Everyone,

quick question: how large does detection probability need to be to obtain a reliable/acceptable abundance estimate using the RN method? Also do you have a reference for this value?

I thought Royle & Nichols stated this in their original paper, but I can't seem to find it.

Thanks,

Pat

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] minimum detection probability
parts:
Dear Pat,

 

Couple of things:

(1)    First, whether you get reliable inference or not in the RN depends a lot on how well the parametric assumptions of this model are met. Or rather, how badly they are violated. The RN model is much more sensitive to the parametric assumptions than many other hierarchical models, such as binomial or multinomial mixture models or occupancy models. ---- Presumably, you can do some GOF test to get a feel for this, though we never know whether the test is sensitive at all or to specific assumption violations, for lack of studies

(2)    When abundance is very high, there may be little or now variation in p with which to estimate variation in abundance

(3)    And then there is the first law of capture-recapture: when p gets small, things become screwy.

 

The last one is actually the simplest and you can explore this using simulation, using exactly your sample sizes (N sites, N visits) and presumed parameter values (abundance and detection). The first one is the most difficult one.

 

Best regards --  Marc

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] minimum detection probability
parts:
Thanks Marc :)

I am currently designing a study which will compare cat abundance between two geographical regions using camera traps. I have recently run a pilot study to get a feel for the probability of detecting cats within each region. As the detection probability from my pilot study was low I plan to put multiple cameras at each sample site within each geographic location and pool detection across all cameras at each sample site to increase detection probability. I am trying to work out how many cameras I need at each site. I have been told by a colleague that my detection probability at each site needs to be at least 0.1 (10%) or higher to obtain reasonable abundance estimates, although I thought I had read that detection probabilities of 0.2 (20%) or higher were needed to obtain reasonable abundance estimates using RN method. The minimum detection probability required to obtain reasonable RN abundance estimates will consequently determine the number of cameras I must have at each site.

Thanks
